events.title: The Finding of the Holy Cross
events.shortBlurb: By ancient tradition St. Helena discovered the True Cross at Jerusalem, a finding long kept on this day…
body: About the year 326 Helena, mother of the Emperor Constantine, made her pilgrimage to the holy places of Jerusalem, where Constantine was clearing away the pagan temple raised over the tomb of Christ. By the tradition recorded by Rufinus and the historians Socrates and Sozomen, her search near Calvary brought to light the wood of the Lord's cross.

Later legend tells that three crosses came to light, the Lord's being known from the thieves' when a dead man revived at its touch. Over the holy places rose the basilica of the Holy Sepulchre, dedicated in 335, and a portion of the wood Helena brought to Rome, where it is venerated to this day in the church of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, once her palace.

The Western Church kept the Finding, or Invention, of the Holy Cross on 3 May, distinct from the Exaltation of the Cross on 14 September, a feast joined also to the relic's recovery from the Persians by the Emperor Heraclius about 629. The May feast was removed from the general Roman calendar in 1960.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “Archæology of the Cross and Crucifix”
